item.text:
**Bottom line:** mostly no. I found rhetorical and narrow regulatory signals about fair competition and innovation, but the strongest 2024 evidence still points to secrecy for powerful firms, patronage, and loyalty-based economic control rather than serious resistance to corruption or oligarchic capture.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak pro, aspirational | Executive Order on Russia's development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets official goals for fair competition, private initiative, higher living standards, and technological effectiveness. This is the clearest pro-market statement, but it is a target list, not evidence that Putin actually curbed corruption or connected-business privilege. | 5B.5; also 5B.1, 5B.4 |
| Weak pro, narrow | Federal Law on an experimental legal regime in digital innovations | President of Russia | 2024-08-08 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Creates a controlled experimental regime that can help some innovation and entrepreneurship. It is supportive of a limited form of market development, but it is tightly supervised and not an anti-corruption reform. | 5B.5; also 5B.4 |
| Against | Putin lets economically significant entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Lets major firms reduce public disclosure, which weakens transparency and external scrutiny. That favors insider control over fair competition and makes connected-business privilege easier to hide. | 5B.5; also 5B.3, 5B.4 |
| Against | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Says corruption is pervasive and the regime distributes economic assets to allies in exchange for loyalty and protection from prosecution. It also describes expropriation risk and pressure on firms to serve state needs. This is direct evidence of patronage and oligarchic capture. | 5B.5; also 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4 |
| Against | Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Describes political centralization, weak local autonomy, and state-aligned institutions, reinforcing the picture of an economy and state structure that rewards loyalty over independent competition. | 5B.5; also 5B.2, 5B.4 |
| Against | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reports growth and low unemployment, but Reuters explicitly ties much of the expansion to military production. That is not evidence of clean competition or resistance to monopolistic, state-driven privilege. | 5B.5; also 5B.1, 5B.4 |

**Assessment**
- The only positive material is aspirational or tightly controlled.
- The dominant pattern is secrecy, state favoritism, and loyalty-based distribution of economic benefits.
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a real anti-corruption or anti-oligarchy campaign that constrained Putin’s insiders.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of major anti-corruption prosecutions targeting politically connected elites, anti-monopoly enforcement against regime-linked firms, or meaningful protection of independent business from state capture.
- The best pro evidence was rhetorical language about fair competition, not observable institutional restraint.
